data.narrative:
Vermeer, a Series A–stage defense and security company founded by Brian Streem, has raised $10M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 11 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies comprising 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers including Anduril Industries, Helsing, and Castelion.

Two triangulation methods are applied. Stage-progression modeling uses the $10M raised as a proxy for post-money valuation and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage transitions, yielding $20M. Peer-median analysis across the 11-company Defense & Security cohort produces a median valuation of $1.0B, with observed range of $125M to $3.0B; sampled peers at Series B (Dream Security at $3.0B, Allen Control Systems at $2.2B, Harmattan AI at $1.4B, Code Metal at $1.2B, and Twenty at $1.0B) anchor the upper portion of this distribution.

The two methods generate a wide but bracketed range: $17M (low, stage-progression floor), $510M (median triangulated), and $1.1B (high, peer-median weighted). Key uncertainties include stage-specific maturation relative to the peer cohort—most comparables trade at Series B or later—and the extent to which Vermeer's current revenue, product maturity, and TAM penetration track relative to the peer median. The wide dispersion reflects genuine ambiguity at seed-to-A inflection points in this sector.
